answer: You have 30 days from the date of discharge to submit a main reimbursement claim [1][2]. However, under the 2024 archived rules, the deadline was 15 days [3], and group claims under corporate plans have a submission window of 60 days from discharge [5].
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3][4].
No, maternity cover is not available on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on retail plans, unless Aurora explicitly waives it in writing on the policy schedule [3]. For the Aurora Senior Care plan for ages 60 and above, the waiting period for a pre-existing disease is 24 months [5].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days [1].
As of 1 April 2026, Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns [1].

On the Aurora Gold plan, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, which accumulates to a maximum of 100% [1]. (Note: Source [5] contains a conflicting overview table stating 50% per year with a max of 200% for Gold [5].)
No, IVF treatment is permanently excluded from coverage [1].
The cataract surgery sub-limit on Gold is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If Aurora's final response is unsatisfactory, or if they have not responded within 30 days of the original complaint, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1]. Additionally, if you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome or receive no response within 15 days, you can escalate the matter to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2].

Aurora Health Insurance provides road ambulance cover of ₹5,000 per hospitalisation across all plans [1]. Additionally, the Aurora Gold plan includes air ambulance cover of ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India, subject to prior authorisation [5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The 30-day initial waiting period applies, but no separate waiting period does [1].
The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3]. Specifically, it is 15 days from receipt, or 30 days for policies sold through distance marketing [1][2].
You receive 150 wellness points for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advancement, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement, and it is distinct from out-patient treatment [3].
A hospital must notify Aurora of an emergency admission for cashless within 24 hours of admission [1][5].
No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a Third Party Administrator (TPA) [1].
To qualify as a hospital, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, not everything will be paid because proportionate deduction applies when you occupy a room costing more than your room-rent limit [1][5]. For a room billed at ₹15,000 per day against a limit of ₹10,000 per day, the eligibility ratio is 0.667, meaning associated charges like surgeon, anaesthetist, nursing, OT, and investigations are scaled down proportionally [1][5]. Only specific items like pharmacy and consumables are paid in full [5].

Dependent parents can be covered on Silver (at an extra premium), Gold, and Platinum plans, while they are not allowed on the Bronze plan [1]. Adding a dependent parent to a floater often costs more than an individual senior-citizen policy for that parent because the premium is determined by the age of the eldest member covered [4].
